solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expect I will go before head after some horseplay

indicators.note: after says the rest of the wordplay follows the horseplay piece
will go before puts the letter I in front of the word for head

parts.note: antics are playful pranks, so one bit of horseplay is an antic
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Someone braces for a head-butt after a bit of rough play.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to look forward to it as likely, a close synonym of expecting it.

clue.text: Teenage trouble spots?

parts.note: reads like places where teenagers get into bother, but the spots are pimples on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rough neighbourhoods where youths cause trouble; the 'spots' are literal blemishes that plague adolescents.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin condition is the classic affliction of adolescence, producing troublesome pimples.

clue.text: It's highly confidential

parts.note: highly confidential is read literally as secret at the highest level, top meaning high

explanation.definitionFit: A security classification for material whose disclosure is most strictly forbidden.

clue.text: Shouts out names

definitions.meaning: to shout out is to cry or call aloud
to name a child is to call it something

explanation.surface: Someone yells out a list of names, like a roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both crying out loudly and giving someone a name, as in 'they call him Bob'.

clue.text: Weak case made for charitable collection

parts.note: poor means weak or feeble, as in a poor effort
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A flimsy container is cobbled together for gathering donations.
explanation.definitionFit: A box in a church where coins for the needy are dropped is a receptacle for charitable giving.

clue.text: Ties the rest in knots

indicators.note: tangled up in knots means the letters of the words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rope-handler binds up the leftover lengths into knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' rearranges THEREST into the answer; knots fit the ties picture, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethers are ropes that tie an animal, and to tether is to tie up, so the verb matches ties.

clue.text: Staunch good man the writer turns over

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

indicators.note: turns over, in a down-style flip, reads the setter's word backwards

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, giving me

explanation.surface: A virtuous man and the author are flipped about, perhaps in a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow of blood is to staunch it: both verbs mean to stop it flowing.

clue.text: Cut of the cloth?

parts.note: the cloth is the clergy, and their cut is the tenth share of produce paid to the church

explanation.walkthrough: 'the cut of one's cloth' sounds like tailoring; here 'the cloth' means the clergy and 'cut' their share.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of income or produce was given to the church, the clergy's portion or cut.

clue.text: Much improved, that enjoys greater popularity

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of approval when something gets better: that's an improvement
read whimsically as a thing that people like more

explanation.surface: Something has got much better and is now more widely liked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when something improves; read literally it describes what is better liked.

clue.text: Official bit of advice goes to teachers, say

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint or piece of advice
a school's teachers are its staff; say marks them as an example

explanation.surface: An official passes a helpful hint on to the teaching body.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer, originally one carrying a metal-tipped staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's or court officer, so an official of the law courts.

clue.text: Plane crashes somewhere in the Himalayas

indicators.note: a plane that crashes is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An aircraft goes down in the high mountains of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This kingdom lies along the Himalayan range and holds Everest, so it is a place in those mountains.

clue.text: In hospital, most would like to go like this tradesman

parts.words: In hospital, most would like to go like this
parts.note: patients wish to leave, out, in better health, fitter

explanation.surface: Most hospital patients hope to leave in better shape than they arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OUT FITTER, it is how a patient wants to leave hospital; whole, it is someone who sells clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shopkeeper selling clothing and equipment, a kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Practical is 'in' — be less fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at an elaborate or fanciful rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that being sensible is fashionable, so cut down on the frills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges INBELESS; 'is' is a link and the quoted 'in' is fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible and practical both describe choices grounded in good sense rather than show.

clue.text: It can be enthralling for a while

definitions.meaning: a magic charm holds its victim enthralled
a ... is a period of time, as in a ... of rain

explanation.surface: Something holds you captivated for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bewitching charm and a short stretch of time, as in a cold spell.

clue.text: Europeans travel by air to obtain a dubious aphrodisiac

parts.note: the Spanish are a European people
to fly is to travel through the air

explanation.surface: People from the continent take a flight in search of a questionable love potion.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish fly is a preparation of dried blister beetles, long sold as a supposed love drug and actually toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: This beetle extract has a reputation as a sexual stimulant, although it is poisonous and unreliable.

clue.text: Hit back with a note before ten? It can be true

indicators.note: with simply joins the a onto the reversed hit
before puts the musical note in front of the numeral
back says the word for hit is read in the other direction

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply
do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A puzzle: strike back, add a note before ten, and wonder whether it all holds true.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a paradox being a seemingly absurd statement that may nonetheless be true.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a self-contradictory-sounding claim that may still turn out to be correct.

clue.text: Dreadful family heard in abusive outburst

indicators.note: heard says the two words are spoken aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: dire means dreadful and a tribe is a family or clan

explanation.surface: An awful family is overheard in the middle of a stream of abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns DIRE TRIBE, spoken, into the answer's sound; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack or tirade, a sustained abusive outburst.

clue.text: Long John Silver's line

parts.note: a person's line is their trade, and the pirate of Treasure Island was employed as a ship's cook

explanation.walkthrough: 'line' suggests a catchphrase like 'Pieces of eight'; it means line of work, and Silver signed on as ship's cook.
explanation.definitionFit: In Treasure Island the pirate Long John Silver serves aboard the Hispaniola as the ship's cook.

clue.text: Welcoming start of treatment, mentions new remedies

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds the other inside
new signals the letters of mentions are made into something fresh
start of takes just the opening letter of the word treatment

explanation.surface: Treatment begins by welcoming patients, and new remedies get a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MENTIONS to OINMENTS, and 'Welcoming' puts the T from 'start of treatment' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments are salves applied to the skin as medicinal remedies.

clue.text: Less than 50 per cent? Certainly!

definitions.meaning: literally a fraction that falls short of a half
the British exclamation meaning 'absolutely!' or 'very much so!'

explanation.surface: A question about a share under half, answered with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'not half!' is an emphatic yes, the opposite of what the words literally say.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means under a half; as British slang it is an enthusiastic 'definitely'.

clue.text: Flier in a flat spin

indicators.note: a flat spin is a state of panic, and spinning the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who is flying is panicking wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flat spin' is a confused panic; 'spin' rearranges INAFLAT. The answer is a breed of pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a fancy pigeon with a fanned tail, so a bird and therefore a flier.

clue.text: Find fee out of order for Turkish official

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone locates a fee charged irregularly by a Turkish functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges FINDFEE. The answer is a former Turkish title of respect for officials and learned men.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a title for an Ottoman official or educated man, a gentleman of rank in Turkey.

clue.text: Creates a secret passage

parts.note: sounds like building a hidden tunnel, but means putting a piece of text into cipher

explanation.walkthrough: The 'passage' is a stretch of writing, not a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher a message is to turn its text into code that only the intended reader understands.

clue.text: Heavenly body, one seen in flight

indicators.note: seen in says the numeral appears inside the word for a celestial body

parts.note: a star is a celestial body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A star, one glimpsed while on a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel to suit the heavenly body; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean a whole series of steps between floors, which is a flight.

clue.text: Silver down but looking healthy

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
low means down in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone with grey hair is feeling down yet looks well.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing face suggests good health, with a rosy colour from exercise.

clue.text: Common title for Satan?

parts.note: the Devil is familiarly called Old Nick, so Nick is his informal title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' is a traditional English name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar informal name used in place of a real one, and the Devil's is Nick.

clue.text: Two Poles about to set up job centre? Untrue

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the poles enclose the next piece

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: set up in a down clue reads the little word upwards, reversing it
centre takes the middle letter of the word job

explanation.surface: Two Polish workers are about to open an employment office, a false claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are compass points, not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: As a retort the phrase denies a claim, meaning that is not the case.

clue.text: Numbers taken out of telephone service

indicators.note: taken out of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Phone numbers are removed from the telephone service.
explanation.definitionFit: Single digits from one to nine are units, so numbers in the plural sense.

clue.text: Pension for all directors?

definitions.meaning: a pension in a French boarding house includes all meals, bed and board
read literally, the whole board of a company

explanation.surface: Who pays retirement income to every member of the company board?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' here is the French boarding-house term, not retirement income.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel terms covering all meals; literally, a complete set of company directors.

clue.text: Fitting end for a piece of wood

definitions.text: Fitting end for a piece of wood

parts.words: Fitting end for a piece of wood
parts.note: fitting means suitable but here is a joint fitting into a mortise

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting end' sounds like an apt fate; it is the projecting end that fits a mortise.
explanation.definitionFit: In joinery this projection on the end of a timber is shaped to slot into a mortise hole.

clue.text: Boat to swing off course to port

parts.note: a ship yaws when it swings off its heading
port is the left side, and L stands for left

explanation.surface: A vessel veers off its heading towards the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel, so a kind of boat.

clue.text: They provide poor accommodation

parts.note: poor accommodation sounds like shoddy lodgings but means lodgings for poor people

explanation.walkthrough: 'poor accommodation' reads as low-quality housing; it means housing for the poor, provided by charity.
explanation.definitionFit: These charitable dwellings were endowed to house elderly or needy people free of rent.
